[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: a variable is a box, so the array's values are 'inside' a. Java rule: the variable a holds only a reference (memory address, pointer) to the array object, which lives elsewhere.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: an array reference, the value of an array variable; it is the memory address of the array, called a pointer.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: a variable of array type holds a reference to an array object; operations on the name itself (assignment, ==, printing) act on that address.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: for a[i], the address stored in a is read, the index i is added (scaled by the element size), and the memory at the resulting address is accessed: two elementary operations.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: the value of a is a reference (printed as hexadecimal). With the array at locations 523..530, a[4] is found at location 523 + 4 = 527.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: assigning a reference (a = b, or a = new ...) changes only which array the variable points to; the arrays themselves are unchanged.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): new reserves the memory and yields the array's address, which the array variable then stores.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): An array variable stores the memory address of the array, not its elements.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: the model that explains constant-time indexing, aliasing, reference equality and printing of arrays.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Conservation: copying a reference keeps one shared array (changes through either name are seen by both); assigning a new reference breaks the link without changing either array.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: reason in terms of references whenever arrays are assigned, compared, printed or passed to methods. Reason in terms of elements when indexing.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A reference must point to an array before it is indexed. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: an array variable holding null (e.g. an element of a String[][] row not yet created, or a field never assigned) is indexed (NullPointerException)
When an array is created, the array name stores the memory address of its values; a[i] is found by adding i to that address.
Declaring an array variable creates only a variable that holds a reference to an array; the array itself is a separate object.
Because an array variable holds a reference, b = a copies the reference, so a and b name the same array.
An array variable stores the memory address of the array, not its elements.
Printing an array variable prints the reference it holds, not the elements.
